groups.name: base
groups.why: the front-end and projection checks, the doc, view and rename controls, the JSON and block refusers, the id table's ordinal-slot controls in C and C++, the float-NaN widening control and the fixed form's run-copy bound in both systems legs beside them: Go, the host C and C++ compilers and the C/C++ serialize siblings, and nothing else. Measured 28 s over 24 controls, plus 16 s for the two C++ ordinal-slot controls and the C rewind control beside them.

groups.name: base-packet
groups.why: the four packet families on the host toolchain, and the wide-scalar controls beside them: each is one small compile off the generated tree, and they share it. Measured 42 s over 22 controls.

groups.name: base-conformance
groups.why: The shared conformance harness controls, including the sabotaged C++ reference. The completed C driver now has three separate compile-heavy groups below; combining them exceeded the five-minute job ceiling on run 34186742566.

groups.name: base-c-conformance
groups.why: The C JSON driver sabotage and the small message/retention compiler probes share one job. The expanded C driver must not share a job with the other two complete C driver rebuilds.

groups.name: base-c-wire
groups.why: The complete C wire roster rebuilt with a permissive LEB reader took about 99 seconds on run 34186742566. Keep that compile in its own job within the control-time budget.

groups.name: base-c-foreign
groups.why: The C foreign-byte-order sabotage rebuilds the complete driver. It was cancelled while compiling after the preceding C controls exhausted the old combined job; isolate it without raising the timeout.

groups.name: base-c-le-trailer
groups.why: the C little-endian memcpy arm of table_writer_finish: overlay-rebuilds the C emitter, regenerates the soak units and requires the host soak golden to go red. Isolated from the other C overlay rebuilds the way base-c-foreign is. Host-only, so it is not on the s390x job that already runs tables-c-big-endian-negative-control. Measured 10 s over 1 control on the author's machine.

groups.name: base-conformance-absence
groups.why: one control, and it is alone because it costs 47 s on the runner: it rebuilds the C++ reference driver under a sabotage the way the group above does, and the two together do not fit the owner's rule in one job. Measured 15 s over 1 control.

groups.name: base-maps
groups.why: the map gate's builder and shape controls, and the cook checker's walk over a map. The family ran as two jobs at 80 s and 74 s of control time on run 34115675206, which is inside the rule and too close to it, so it runs as four. Measured 20 s over 5 controls.

groups.name: base-maps-depth
groups.why: the map gate's depth, duplicate, entry-node and fit controls. Measured 19 s over 4 controls.

groups.name: base-maps-keys
groups.why: the map gate's four key controls: the domain, the identity, the kind and the length. Measured 19 s over 4 controls.

groups.name: base-maps-order
groups.why: the map gate's placement, ordering and reset controls. Measured 19 s over 5 controls.

groups.name: base-lists
groups.why: the list gate, whole, with the umbrella target that names every leaf: make builds each of them once in one invocation, so the umbrella costs this group nothing and stays on the leg. The cook tool's list control rides here for the same corpus. Measured 35 s over 14 controls.

groups.name: base-arms
groups.why: the union-arm traversal gate, whole, with the umbrella target that names every leaf: make builds each of them once in one invocation, so the umbrella costs this group nothing and stays on the leg. Measured 16 s over 8 controls.

groups.name: base-shared-node
groups.why: the shared-node control and the two Go fuzz controls, which read the same walk the arm gate does and are 82 s of control time beside it on run 34115675206. Measured 17 s over 3 controls.

groups.name: base-cook
groups.why: the cook's controls, the blob span and read hooks, and the C leg's fuzz, soak and keyed refusal: one cooked corpus, built once, that every one of them reads. Measured 34 s over 11 controls.

groups.name: base-keyed
groups.why: the keyed-collection controls. The iteration control is the long one. Measured 17 s over 3 controls.

groups.name: base-keyed-shift
groups.why: the keyed shift control and the flat-wire one, which are 76 s of control time beside the group above on run 34115675206. Measured 12 s over 2 controls.

groups.name: base-pack
groups.why: the pack golden's framing control: elide a present `?T` in the Go encoder and the byte comparison against the C++ Save has to go red. Measured 7 s off one warm build.

groups.name: base-hostile
groups.why: the JSON number grammar's hostile-value control, alone. Its floor is the SANITIZED build of the hostile-value driver, which no other control shares, and the two pack controls in one job were 81 s of control time in a 113 s job on run 34120798793, the tightest job in the leg. Measured 14 s off one warm build.

groups.name: message-form
groups.why: the message form's blades: the count, the emitter, the text content rule, the blob one, and the form-2 retain capture. The one control of this family that drives 49 sabotage rows one submake each does not fit the owner's rule alone, so it runs nightly. Measured 16 s over 5 controls.

groups.name: table-distinctness
groups.why: the id table's distinctness control, alone, because it is an overlay rebuild: it patches the C++ table emitter's probe, rebuilds the compiler under the overlay, regenerates one unit and requires the distinctness gate to go red on the probe's own cases. It costs what the other overlay rebuilds cost, without the fuzzer's pass on top. Measured about 30 s over 1 control on the author's machine.

groups.name: wire-fuzz
groups.why: the tolerant-wire oracle and node-type controls, which read a pinned vector rather than rebuilding the compiler. The five oracles ran as one job at 82 s of control time on run 34115675206, most of it the fuzz driver they all build, so they run as two. Measured 11 s over 2 controls.

groups.name: wire-fuzz-message-oracle
groups.why: the tolerant-wire oracles for the message form's text and blob records, and the retain one. Measured 3 s over 3 controls.

groups.name: wire-fuzz-length
groups.why: one control per job. Each of these rebuilds the compiler under a source overlay and then runs the fuzzer over the sabotaged wire, which is 55 s to 75 s on the runner, so two of them in one job miss the owner's rule. Measured 23 s on the author's machine and 59 s on the runner.

groups.why: one control per job. Each of these rebuilds the compiler under a source overlay and then runs the fuzzer over the sabotaged wire, which is 55 s to 75 s on the runner, so two of them in one job miss the owner's rule. Measured 22 s on the author's machine and 58 s on the runner.

groups.name: wire-fuzz-wide-text
groups.why: one control per job. Each of these rebuilds the compiler under a source overlay and then runs the fuzzer over the sabotaged wire, which is 55 s to 75 s on the runner, so two of them in one job miss the owner's rule. Measured 28 s on the author's machine and 75 s on the runner.

groups.name: wire-fuzz-message-text
groups.why: one control per job. Each of these rebuilds the compiler under a source overlay and then runs the fuzzer over the sabotaged wire, which is 55 s to 75 s on the runner, so two of them in one job miss the owner's rule. Measured 22 s on the author's machine.

groups.name: wire-fuzz-message-blob
groups.why: one control per job. Each of these rebuilds the compiler under a source overlay and then runs the fuzzer over the sabotaged wire, which is 55 s to 75 s on the runner, so two of them in one job miss the owner's rule. Measured 22 s on the author's machine.

groups.name: wire-fuzz-retain-class
groups.why: one control per job. Each of these rebuilds the compiler under a source overlay and then runs the fuzzer over the sabotaged wire, which is 55 s to 75 s on the runner, so two of them in one job miss the owner's rule. Measured 29 s on the author's machine.

groups.name: block-fuzz
groups.why: the block fuzz extent oracle, which sabotages the C++, C# and Rust block emitters together and then requires all three fuzzers to go red, so one job needs both the .NET SDK and cargo. Measured 48 s on the runner.

groups.name: block-fuzz-maximum
groups.why: the block fuzz maximum oracle, the extent oracle's twin, in a job of its own because the two together are 81 s of control time on top of two SDK installs. Measured 33 s on the runner.

groups.name: cs
groups.why: the C# port's conformance leg and its four packet families. Measured 13 s over 5 controls, on a host carrying no such SDK, so that is a floor and not the job's cost: it is the work up to the point the SDK is first reached.

groups.name: cs-cook
groups.why: the cook-open gates whose instrument is the C# reader, and the two block controls that only compile. Measured 24 s on the runner.

groups.name: cs-block-layout
groups.why: the block layout model control, alone: it moves an offset in the compiler's model and requires both the C++ static_asserts and the C# once-run layout check to go red, which is 39 s on the runner.

groups.name: cs-block-pitch
groups.why: the block padding and pitch controls, whose instrument is the same C# layout check as the group above and which cost 31 s and 29 s on the runner.

groups.name: rust
groups.why: the Rust port's name gate and its four packet families. Measured 3 s over 5 controls, on a host carrying no such SDK, so that is a floor and not the job's cost.

groups.name: js
groups.why: the JavaScript port's controls, the packet arm-default oracle's two JS legs, and the three newer packet families: ten controls after the previous-form table legs were removed. Measured 9 s over 13 controls before that, on a host carrying no such SDK, so that is a floor and not the job's cost.

groups.name: dart
groups.why: the Dart port's controls and its four packet families: seven controls after the previous-form table legs were removed. Measured 5 s over 10 controls before that, on a host carrying no such SDK, so that is a floor and not the job's cost.

groups.name: java
groups.why: the Java port's controls and its four packet families: eight controls, the eighth being the FIXED FORM's (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §3.4), which writes one text length a byte too high and must red the C++ reference's byte match. Measured 6 s over 10 controls before the previous-form table legs were removed, on a host carrying no such SDK, so that is a floor and not the job's cost.

groups.name: elixir
groups.why: the Elixir port's controls and its three packet families. Measured 1 s over 5 controls, on a host carrying no such SDK, so that is a floor and not the job's cost.

groups.name: nightly
groups.why: the one control that does not fit the owner's rule for CI that runs per commit, on its own, at any group size: tables-message-form-negative-control drives 49 sabotage rows one submake each, 124 s on the runner where the rule is 120. The message form's four blades run on the pull request, so what moves nightly is this one pass and nothing else. The group stays a group even at one target, because it is the place a control lands the day it outgrows the rule. certify.yml runs this tier on the schedule it already carries.

groups.name: go-containers
groups.why: Go generated runtime controls: containers, block fill races, caller allocation ownership and the pinned managed allocation floor, bounded retention, and the FIXED FORM's byte oracle against the C++ reference's own corpus (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §3.4).

groups.name: base-reference-review
groups.why: compiled native and sanitizer regressions for variable wide closure, list extent and flags/map widening accounting; seven bounded emitter controls

groups.name: go-view
groups.why: the compiled Go unit registry and packet descriptor boundary controls

excluded.reason: an alias that re-invokes make once per language for the nine packet-arm-defaults-<lang>-negative-control targets, every one of which this leg already runs in its own toolchain group. Running the alias too would need all seven SDKs on one runner to prove a second time what seven parallel jobs prove once.

a parameterized worker with no sabotage of its own: it reads SABOTAGE, SABOTAGE_FILE and SABOTAGE_TEST from the command line, and tables-message-form-negative-control, which the nightly tier runs, drives it once for each of its 49 sabotage rows. Invoked bare it has nothing to break.

an umbrella over the seventeen map-gate leaves, which the base-maps and base-maps-keys groups run between them. The family is too long for one job under the owner's rule, and an umbrella in either half would re-run the other half's eight or nine controls to prove a second time what the other job proves once.

an umbrella over the twelve tolerant-wire leaves, which the wire-fuzz groups run between them. Each leaf rebuilds the compiler under an overlay and costs 55 s to 75 s on the runner, so they run one per job; the umbrella in any one of them would re-run all twelve and take the job to six minutes.

an umbrella over the two retain leaves, tables-wire-fuzz-retain-oracle-negative-control and tables-wire-fuzz-retain-class-negative-control, which the wire-fuzz-message-oracle and wire-fuzz-retain-class groups run between them. It carries no recipe of its own, so the umbrella in either group re-runs the other group's leaf to prove a second time what that job proves once.

the body of ci.yml's big-endian job, which runs it on every pull request already: the job cross-compiles the tables battery for s390x, runs it under qemu and then compiles it a second time for this control. Issue #684 owns moving that job, so the control is named here rather than placed in a group, and this leg does not cross-compile it a second time.

the C twin of tables-big-endian-negative-control: ci.yml's big-endian job runs it on every pull request already, after the C++ put16 control. It overlay-rebuilds the C emitter, regenerates the soak units and cross-compiles the C soak for s390x so a host-order table_writer_finish fallback turns the golden gate red. Issue #684 owns the job's budget, so the control is named here rather than placed in a group.
